items.title: From Waste Picking to Self-Reliance:
items.summary: Mekala Yesamma’s Journey towards Economic Empowerment 06 OCT 2026 7:58PM by PIB Delhi Financial assistance can play an important role in helping individuals from disadvantaged communities establish sustainable livelihoods and improve their economic condition. Timely support for self-employment can create new income opportunities, strengthen family financial security and promote greater dignity in livelihood.

facts.text: Ms. Mekala Yesamma, aged 33, belongs to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community and had been working as a waste picker in the Guntur Municipal Corporation for nearly 12 years.
The total project cost was Rs. 16,99,952, supported by a loan of Rs. 10,24,964 and capital subsidy of Rs. 6,74,988.
Before receiving the assistance, Ms. Yesamma earned approximately Rs. 8,000 per month through waste-picking activities.
With the support provided under the SUY scheme and the resulting livelihood opportunity, she now earns an additional Rs. 10,000 per month, taking her total monthly income to approximately Rs. 18,000.

bullets: Constitutional basis: Art. 243K (panchayats) and 243ZA (municipalities). It superintends, directs and controls electoral rolls and all local body polls, including republishing Gram Panchayat rolls.
Post-bifurcation, the Governor constituted the State Election Commission for AP on 30 January 2016.

AP: Anil Chandra Punetha appointed State Election Commissioner (APPCA, Apr 2026). He ordered photo electoral rolls for the MPTC/ZPTC polls (TH, 8 Sep 2026) and ward rolls for 41 ULBs (12 corporations, 29 municipalities and nagar panchayats) for publication on 22 Sep 2026 (TH, 16 Sep 2026).
Article 243ZA gives the same SEC the municipal elections - so the SEC conducts local body elections (not State Legislature, not cooperative societies).
A separate constitutional SEC ended States' power to postpone local polls indefinitely.

items.title: STRONG DEMOCRACIES ARE BUILT ON DIALOGUE, DIVERSE VIEWS AND MEANINGFUL PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
items.summary: Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla emphasised that strong democracies are built on dialogue, diverse views and meaningful public participation.

facts.text: Noting that legislatures are forum for discussion, dialogue, debate and exchange of diverse views, he mentioned that democracy becomes stronger when there is space for agreement as well as disagreement, and when diverse perspectives are brought into the legislative process.

He congratulated the present and former Chief Ministers, Speakers, Ministers, Members of Parliament and Members of the Goa Legislative Assembly who have contributed to the State's socio-economic development over the past 25 years.

Shri Birla noted that the Silver Jubilee should not merely be an occasion to celebrate the Assembly's achievements of the past 25 years, but should also provide an opportunity to envision the next 25 years.

He conveyed his greetings to all present and former Members, Speakers, Chief Ministers and other public representatives who have contributed to the development of Goa and strengthened the democratic institutions of the State.

items.title: An Approach Paper on Expanding the scope and coverage for the Index of Services Production
items.summary: MoSPI invites comments/ feedback from stakeholders on the Approach Paper 06 OCT 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi The services sector has firmly established itself as the primary engine of India's economic growth, driving more than half of the national Gross Value Added (GVA).

facts.text: The initial framework tracks 19 broad service sub-sectors—relying on high-frequency administrative data sources and data of outward supplies from GST which collectively accounted for approximately 60 per cent of services-sector GVA.
Together, these three vital sectors represent nearly 21 per cent of services GVA for the 2024–25 period.
By successfully incorporating them, MoSPI will elevate the total coverage of the monthly ISP to approximately 78.4 per cent of the entire services-sector GVA.

items.title: Raksha Mantri launches first indigenous Fleet Support Ship ‘ Surya’ at Hindustan Shipyard Ltd in Visakhapatnam
items.summary: The milestone is a significant step in strengthening HSL’s capacity to build larger and more complex ships and advancing India’s indigenous maritime capability. Addressing the gathering, the Raksha Mantri said the three milestones had significance beyond the individual achievements.

facts.text: Recalling the launch of the first ship built in independent India ‘Jala Usha’ at Visakhapatnam in 1948, RM highlighted India’s longstanding maritime heritage, noting that the country’s relationship with the sea dates back to ancient times.

Designed and built indigenously by HSL, the Fleet Support Ships will feature enhanced cargo and fluid capacity, onboard first-line maintenance workshops, a helicopter deck for Multi-Role Helicopter operations and self-defence systems.

He said the State’s MSMEs could become suppliers, universities could contribute to research and skill development, technology companies could support digital shipbuilding and startups could develop maritime technologies.
RM also stressed the need for an integrated national maritime ecosystem involving the Navy, HSL, DRDO, academia, industry, MSMEs and startups.

items.title: India, Switzerland Strengthen Strategic Science & Technology Partnership; Dr. Jitendra Singh Holds Bilateral Meeting with Swiss President Guy Parmelin
items.summary: Guy Parmelin, in New Delhi, with discussions focused on further strengthening the longstanding India-Switzerland partnership in science, technology, research and innovation. The meeting focused on taking the bilateral S&T partnership into a more structured and long-term phase, with greater institutional engagement and cooperation in emerging areas of mutual interest.

facts.text: He also welcomed the Letter of Intent between the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and the Department of Science & Technology (DST) and the Implementation Agreement between the Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW) and DST, and said these initiatives would further strengthen instit…

Recalling the bilateral Science and Technology Agreement signed in 2003, he said the partnership has grown steadily and that Switzerland is committed to developing a more structured and long-term framework for cooperation.

President Parmelin said Switzerland has earmarked a further CHF 45 million for the partnership, and expressed the expectation of a corresponding commitment from India to further strengthen and consolidate the joint Indo-Swiss research framework.
India and Switzerland have built more than two decades of cooperation in Science and Technology since the signing of the Inter-Governmental Agreement in 2003.

bullets: Repo (MPC), SDF, MSF, bank rate, reverse repo, CRR, SLR: Set by each bank PLR/BPLR (old), Base Rate (1 Jul 2010), MCLR (1 Apr 2016), spread over EBLR; Market-determined Call money rate (WACR), TREPS, T-bill and G-sec yields
EBLR: from 1 Oct 2019, new floating-rate personal/retail and MSE loans must be linked to an external benchmark. Options: repo, 3-month or 6-month T-bill yield, or an FBIL-published rate (APP).
Trap: SLR and CRR are set by RBI, not by banks; MCLR is each bank's internal benchmark.
Purpose of MCLR (UPSC 2016: both statements correct): more transparency in how banks fix rates, and faster transmission of policy rates to borrowers.

Draft RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026: proposed to take effect from 1 April 2027. It covers banks, RRBs, co-operative banks, AIFIs and NBFCs/HFCs. Floating-rate personal and MSME loans stay tied to an external benchmark, with interest on the daily reducing balance (LENSD, 14 Aug 2026).

items.title: DRDO Conducts Maiden Live Jump of Advanced High-Altitude Parachute
items.summary: 06 OCT 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the maiden live jump of the Advanced High-Altitude Parachute (AHAP) at one of the highest-altitude drop zones, Nyoma (Mudh DZ). The jump was executed at 16,000 feet above mean sea level (AMSL). The parachute was deployed at 15500 feet AMSL and landing was undertaken at Nyoma (Mudh DZ) which is at 13,700 feet.

facts.text: 06 OCT 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the maiden live jump of the Advanced High-Altitude Parachute (AHAP) at one of the highest-altitude drop zones, Nyoma (Mudh DZ).
Designed and developed by Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE), Agra, AHAP is a static line parachute system for mass drop of paratroopers.

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh complimented DRDO, Defence Forces, DPSUs and Industry on the successful maiden live jump of AHAP indigenous parachute system and termed it as another big step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D & Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh congratulated the team members associated with the design and development of the system.

items.summary: Describing the milestone as a significant achievement in India’s aerospace journey, he called for strengthening indigenous capabilities in the design, development, testing, manufacturing and maintenance of advanced aero-engines, stressing that mastery of propulsion technology is essential for self-reliance in the aerospace and defence sector.

facts.text: Congratulating the engineers, technicians, scientists and skilled workforce of HAL Koraput, Shri Rajnath Singh said the delivery of 2,000 engines represents 2,000 significant contributions to the operational capability of the Defence Forces and reflects six decades of engineering expertise and te…

He highlighted the proposed investment of around Rs 5,000 crore, indigenisation of raw materials in partnership with Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI) and establishment of India’s first indigenous high-thrust engine testing facility.

Despite global supply-chain disruptions and raw-material challenges, HAL delivered the first engine ahead of schedule and has delivered 63 engines against a target of 60 by the end of the second year.
Raksha Mantri announced that HAL is enhancing annual AL-31FP production capacity from 30 to 50 engines with an investment of Rs 335 crore.

items.title: DRDO Conducts Flight Trial of High-Altitude Platform
items.summary: 06 OCT 2026 3:33PM by PIB Delhi Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has carried out the successful flight trial of indigenously developed High-Altitude Platform (HAPS). The experimental flight attained an altitude of 21 km above mean sea level (AMSL) and remained at an altitude of 20 km AMSL for more than 30 minutes, before it was commanded to descend back to ground.

facts.text: 06 OCT 2026 3:33PM by PIB Delhi Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has carried out the successful flight trial of indigenously developed High-Altitude Platform (HAPS).

The experimental flight attained an altitude of 21 km above mean sea level (AMSL) and remained at an altitude of 20 km AMSL for more than 30 minutes, before it was commanded to descend back to ground.

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has complimented DRDO, IAF, PSUs and Industry on successful flight trial of High-Altitude Platform and stated that the successful trial is an important milestone in India’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat journey towards realizing a long endurance stratospheric Airship.
Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh has congratulated the teams associated with the flight trial of high-altitude airship platform.

Water Security gets highest share with 128 works The Water Security pillar comprises 128 works, the highest among the four categories.
The share of livelihood-related works rises substantially, accounting for 26 per cent of the total permissible works under the new framework, compared with 1.1 per cent under the previous framework.

38 works dedicated to Disaster Preparedness and Climate Resilience For the first time, a dedicated category for disaster preparedness and extreme weather events has been incorporated into the rural works framework, comprising 38 works.

items.title: Cabinet approves Commitment of Rs.10,000 Crore towards establishment of the SME Growth Fund for direct equity investments in Small and Medium Enterprises to create future champions
items.summary: This was in part of the holistic set of announcements that were made in Union Budget 2026-27 focussing on providing equity, liquidity and professional support for the MSME ecosystem as a whole. There are existing funds which provide equity support but majority of them focus on early-stage enterprises and cover majorly Micro enterprises.

facts.text: While various initiatives have enhanced access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital required by enterprises seeking to scale, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions, and transform into industry leaders.

The Government expects the Fund to accelerate the emergence of a strong pipeline of Indian companies with the scale, innovation capability, and competitiveness required to become champions in their respective sectors.
Under the initiative, the Government of India will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs.10,000 crore to the Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework.

Investments across industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, will support balanced regional industrial development, reinforce local supply chains and generate high-quality employment opportunities.

bullets: Art. 329(a): laws on delimitation and allotment of seats cannot be questioned in court; Art. 329(b): an election can be challenged only by an election petition .

By convention courts do not interfere once the poll process begins; the ECI cannot review a result. Petitions go to the High Court (Parliament, state legislatures) and the Supreme Court for President/VP (Art. 71) (UPSC).

Art. 329(b): an election to Parliament or a state legislature can be questioned only by an election petition under the RPA 1951. Such petitions are tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court .
President/VP election disputes: decided by the Supreme Court (Art. 71) .
The ECI does not try election petitions. It decides party and symbol disputes and advises on disqualification.

items.title: Chang’e-6 moon soil reveals metallic iron never seen before in lunar samples
items.summary: Recent analysis of lunar soil samples returned by China's Chang’e-6 mission revealed a unique form of iron. This iron, γ-Fe, exhibits exceptional magnetic properties, which could provide insights into the Moon's ancient magnetic field. Researchers suggest that extreme impacts on the lunar surface caused the formation and preservation of this unusual iron.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-5 › Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation › Backward Classes in the Constitution
bullets: "Backward Classes" is not defined in the Constitution (APPSC G2 2017 key: the "defined" statement is the wrong one).

27% OBC quota in central jobs from 1993; in central educational institutions under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, in force Jan 2007 (IYB 2026 says 2007) after the 2005 amendment to Art. 15 (IYB) [GK for the Act's year].

Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (in force 2007): 27% OBC seats in central institutions (IYB; GS 2007 key: 93rd Amendment); OBC = classes "so determined by the Central Government" (APP).

sections.topic: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

sections.topic: Transgender persons · Reservation and state measures

bullets: Debate: NALSA (2014) asked governments to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward (a vertical OBC-type quota); the community seeks horizontal reservation cutting across SC/ST/OBC/General. The issue resurfaced in June 2023 with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the Bombay High Court (APPSC 2022).
Karnataka - first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services (July 2021) (APPSC 2023).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions; CBI and its legal basis › Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 amendments to RTI
bullets: DPDP Act 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act to exempt personal information outright, removing the public-interest override . The Congress president said it "diluted the RTI Act's public interest clause" (TH, 31 Jan 2026).

Economic Survey 2025-26 called for a "re-examination" of the RTI Act. It suggested exempting confidential service records and draft policy discussions, and floated a possible "ministerial veto" (TH, 31 Jan 2026).

bullets: Art. 72 President: pardon incl. death sentence and court-martial .
Art. 161 Governor: cannot pardon a death sentence, but can commute/remit/suspend .
Shatrughan Chauhan v UOI (2014): inordinate, unexplained delay in deciding mercy petitions is a ground to commute death to life .
Also: solitary confinement before rejection is illegal; 14 days between rejection and execution .
Epuru Sudhakar v Govt of AP (2006): pardon/remission is open to limited judicial review .

sections.topic: Sources of institutional finance for AP farmers
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Institutional credit to agriculture in Andhra Pradesh - banks, NABARD and SHGs › Sources of institutional finance for AP farmers
bullets: AP farmers borrow from commercial banks, RRBs and PACS, i.e. all of them (PYQ 2008). Other formal sources are SHGs/JLGs, microfinance and KCC.
Nationally, scheduled commercial banks give over 70% of formal farm credit. The cooperative system (PACS-DCCB-SCB) gives short-term credit, and ARDBs give long-term credit (LENS Apr 2026).
AP Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 review (Jan 2026): Rs 2.96 lakh crore disbursed to agriculture and allied sectors, Rs 1,490 crore to tenant farmers and Rs 95,714 crore to MSMEs (TH, 24 Jan 2026).
Formal credit excludes many tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers because it needs land records. A NABARD Guntur study found formal interest rates of about 2.5-10%.
KCC (1998, NABARD model scheme on the R.V. Gupta Committee): RBI's revised KCC Directions of 19 Jun 2026 apply to loans from 1 Jan 2027, with a maximum tenure of 6 years (earlier 5).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Indian agriculture - importance, land use classification, cropping seasons and cropping pattern › Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings
bullets: India, 10th Agriculture Census (2015-16): 146 million holdings with an average size of 1.08 ha, down from 2.28 ha in 1971. Small and marginal holdings make up 86.2% of holdings but only 47.3% of the area (APPCA; UPSC).
Size classes above are the standard Agriculture Census classes ; "small and marginal farmers" = holdings up to 2 ha.
Tenth Agriculture Census 2015-16 (still the standard all-India reference): 146 million operational holdings, average size 1.08 ha, down from 2.28 ha in 1971 - fragmentation (APPCA 2026).
Small and marginal farmers are about 86.2% of all farmers but hold only about 47% of the crop area (APPCA, May 2026).
Eleventh Agriculture Census 2021-22: provisional State results out; All-India 2021-22 figures are not yet the standard reference.

bullets: Art. 243K (243ZA for municipalities): SEC appointed by the Governor, removable only like a High Court judge; service conditions cannot be varied to the SEC's disadvantage (APPCA, Apr 2026) [GK for last point].
